      "observations": [
        "All 21 owned paths and the full 978-line diff were read. Production search labels, delayed startup, enterprise policies, extension overrides, preferences and LinkHelper switch from Services.search to an imported SearchService provider. The 11 extension-menu test files await that provider's init in setup; the enterprise tests switch the same receiver in reset, engine lookup, defaults, removal, settings persistence, charset and suggestion checks.",
        "The provider import points to the upstream SearchService.sys.mjs, whose implementation/export/wrapping contract was not read as paired engine proof. This comm port establishes its actual import/call sites, not singleton allocation internals, API equivalence for every call or a reproduced spaces-toolbar cure.",
        "Readiness contracts remain distinct. Main-window delayed startup calls init without awaiting it. The extension searchInitialized getter only checks isInitialized or observes init-complete. Default-provider setup awaits it; onManifestEntry deliberately does not await the overall provider work and tracks eventual completion. Nondefault providers follow a separate add path.",
        "Reuse the existing canChangeToConfigEngine versus canInstallEngine caller lesson after checking the exact current branches. The first can set a default independently of the second deciding whether to install; no upstream allowlist/config decision is newly established.",
        "openWebSearch returns the initialization/default-engine lookup chain, then asks openLinkExternally to load the submission URI and records usage. The external helper does not return a navigation-completion promise. Its JSDoc has no summary or promise-completion description; do not infer successful page loading from this caller's resolution.",
        "Keep later accepted API phases separate: test reset is now SearchService.reset rather than wrappedJSObject.reset, extension installation uses singular addEngineFromExtension rather than the owned plural method, and enterprise policy now returns the initialization chain and uses SearchService.CHANGE_REASON. The original port's policy callback did not return that chain. Preferences updateWebSearch still schedules init.then without returning or awaiting it.",
        "No new assertion is added by this port. Changed direct policy assertion expressions retain expected-behavior messages in the inspected hunks; extension menu changes affect setup, not their unchanged assertion bodies. The policy helper separately awaits init and the settings-written notification; existing waitForTick steps are inherited, not new evidence of runtime success.",
        "Manual style checks distinguish script-global getters from lazy module getters and test setup roles. Some added XPCOMUtils bindings have no later direct reference in their exact files, while shared-script consumers are not fully mapped; no unused-binding lint defect is claimed. No global import-style rule follows from the port.",
        "Complete primary Bug 2011723 records the author's attribution of the disappearing spaces toolbar to the search-service replacement. It supplies no independently reproduced cause or runtime cure. Upstream Bug 2000685 remains a bounded unread engine locator.",
        "D279920's complete creation-to-final timeline and all four actual submitted inline bodies were read, including old diff 1188781. Reviewer mkmelin requested moving SearchService into the existing shared-script ChromeUtils.defineESModuleGetters(this) bindings to avoid shared declaration collisions; the author said both were fixed. The owned diff and accepted headers establish that adoption.",
        "The post-landing xpcshell comment suggests direct importESModule when setup needs the module and notes XPCOMUtils. Accepted test_policy_search_engine.js still retains the lazy SearchService getter and XPCOMUtils import. This is scoped feedback, not an adopted global rule or a claimed lint failure. Historical Try links, remote-build events and acceptance remain separate from fresh execution."
